title: The caller keeps the promise after the cache drops its reference
takeaway: The old load can deliver its value, but it cannot restore the cleared cache entry.
assumptions: This example starts with a cache miss at epoch 0. The loader succeeds after clear(). P names the promise returned by read(). Vertical spacing shows order, not elapsed time.

entities.label: Caller
entities.summary: Holds the promise returned by read(). Its reference remains valid after the cache clears pending.

entities.label: Revision cache
entities.summary: Owns epoch, saved, and pending. clear() also resets priorities and byte accounting.

entities.label: Asynchronous loader
entities.summary: Returns a promise for file contents. clear() has no call that cancels this work.

relationships.label: Request file contents
relationships.summary: A cache-miss read starts the illustrated operation.

relationships.label: Start load
relationships.summary: read() captures epoch before it calls load().

relationships.label: Return P
relationships.summary: The cache stores P in pending and returns that same promise to the caller.

relationships.label: Complete successfully
relationships.summary: The completion handler receives the value. A different epoch blocks its saved write.

relationships.label: Resolve P
relationships.summary: The handler returns the loaded value even when the generation check blocks storage.

plan.question: Who receives the old result after clear(), and why can it not enter the cache?
plan.visualApproach: Use three fixed sequence lanes: Caller, Revision cache, and Asynchronous loader. Read downward from read() to result delivery. Show the caller’s retained promise separately from the cache’s pending reference.
plan.whyThisForm: The sequence keeps operation order and ownership visible together. The clear() step removes only the cache reference; the later result crosses the same component boundary.
plan.encodings: Columns identify owners. Downward position shows order. Solid arrows show calls or result delivery. The cache state panel marks the epoch change and removed pending reference. The storage panel shows the unequal generations.
plan.motion: Use a static sequence because all ordered events and retained references fit in one view. Motion would hide earlier evidence that the reader needs to compare ownership before and after clear().
plan.prediction: If clear() runs before another successful pending load completes, its caller can receive the value without that completion adding a saved entry.
plan.restingState: The full sequence keeps the returned promise, clear(), generation mismatch, and successful delivery visible.

scenarios.title: A successful old load completes after clear()
scenarios.input: A cache-miss read captures epoch 0; clear() advances the cache to epoch 1 before the loader completes.

frames.title: Delivery continues; storage is blocked
frames.caption: The caller keeps P. Removing the cache’s pending reference does not cancel the loader or reject P.
